summary: Parallel ingress splay causing tenant 429 waves — configuration and mitigation guidance
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports periodic waves of 429s across a small set of tenant API keys during a scheduled orchestrated ingest. Pattern appears when multiple workers start concurrently and hit the same route.

Impact:
- CloudSync reports intermittent failed uploads and increased client-side retries for ~2-3 minutes during their nightly flush window.
- Affects critical nightly ingestion; partial data loss observed when retries hit overall tenant quota.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool, prod-us-west, tenant: cloudsync-prod, route: /v1/embeddings/bulk
- Client orchestrator runs 32 parallel workers that start a flush at roughly the same time (cron-triggered).

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Schedule orchestrator to start flush at HH:00.
2) 32 workers open HTTP2 multiplexed connections and begin multipart uploads within 6s.
3) Approximately 10-25% of initial requests receive 429s within first 20s, then cascading failures as client retries spin.

Observed behavior:
- 429s spike correlates to the first 20-40 seconds of flush.
- Support headers show token-window exhaustion on a tenant-level burst pool.
- Console shows burst credit drain with refill lag.

Expected behavior:
- Graceful acceptance of staggered concurrent flushes when possible via burst pooling, or clear guidance to client to splay starts to avoid tenant-wide quota exhaustion.

Attachments/Logs:
- Customer provided request timeline and support headers (attached) and a pcap of initial 60s.
- Sampling link to internal metrics (redwood dash): /dash/tenant/cloudsync-prod/rate-limiter/2026-03-09/00:00-01:00
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (reporter): Initial report received from CloudSync support. They requested recommendations that avoid large client-side refactor.

2026-03-10 - Marco Ruiz (support): Acknowledged, requested customer send sample support headers and the orchestrator start timing. Asked for number of parallel connections and whether they use short-lived keys.
2026-03-10 - CloudSync engineer (via email): Confirmed 32 workers, 2 connections per worker (HTTP2), short-lived ephemeral keys rotated every hour. Attached CSV of timestamps and X-RateLimit headers.

2026-03-11 - Marco Ruiz (support): Initial analysis: tenant burst pool depleted quickly due to near-simultaneous token consumption. Noted refill window alignment and HTTP2 multiplexing can amplify apparent concurrency. Requested SRE to analyze allocator traces.

2026-03-11 - Evelyn Chen (SRE): Investigation started. Captured allocator logs and burst-accounting traces for tenant cloudsync-prod. Observed refill epoch jitter ~300-700ms and a sawtooth drain pattern coincident with orchestrator starts.

2026-03-11 - Evelyn Chen (SRE): Hypothesis: orchestrator start alignment combined with ephemeral key fanout and HTTP2 connection reuse causes token-slice fragmentation leading to early tenant exhaustion. Suggested short-term customer-side splay and enabling an isolated burst lane as a mitigation on dedicated pool.
2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz (support): Sent detailed mitigation steps to customer and recommended configuration changes. Waiting for customer verification of reduced failure rate after splay applied.

2026-03-12 - CloudSync engineer: Implemented 8-12s randomized splay across worker starts and reported immediate reduction in 429 spikes. Follow-up asks for recommended long-term config for dedicated pools.
2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz: Advised long-term options and created linked internal task to propose telemetry changes for detecting aligned-start waves automatically.
investigation_notes: Collected rate-limiter allocator trace (trace id rl-20260311-0042). Key observations: tenant burst credits consumed in first 6s; refill notices logged but effective refill applied at next epoch boundary resulting in ~700ms of sustained exhaustion.

HTTP2 multiplexing: connections carried many parallel streams; edge token-slicing logic assigned per-stream shares which, when multiple short-lived ephemeral keys were used, caused double-counting in a small window due to NAT/proxy affinity.

Ephemeral key rotation: rotation during churn amplified allocation thrash—many keys opened and closed across the same refill epoch which misaligns per-key slices and creates transient pressure on tenant pool.

Observed that dedicated pool had a default burst-isolation threshold disabled for this tenant (config shows burst_isolation=false), allowing background probes and flushes to draw from same burst budget.
Reproducibility: reproduced locally by launching 32 parallel clients within 5s using same token refresh pattern; 20% of requests returned 429 within first 20s, matching customer report.
Telemetry gaps: current alerting does not flag aligned-start waves; need a signal for high initial drain rate within first N seconds of a tenant flush job.
resolution_notes: Customer verified workaround: added randomized splay of 8-12s to worker start which substantially reduced immediate 429 spikes. Recommended as short-term fix.

Support recommendations provided to customer (long-form): 1) Add client-side jitter (8-15s) and exponential backoff on retry; 2) If possible, rotate start windows across hosts rather than simultaneous cron; 3) For dedicated tenants, request enabling burst_isolation=true to separate background probes from interactive/bulk burst budget; 4) Consider provisioning a slightly larger committed burst pool for nightly flush windows or scheduling staggered sub-windows.

Config change applied (internal suggestion): enable burst_isolation for cloudsync-prod and add route-level priority class for /v1/embeddings/bulk to limit background credit bleed. Raised internal RFC for a safe rollout pathway.

Follow-up tasks: create an automation rule to detect "aligned-start wave" patterns and recommend splay to customers via console hints; add telemetry counters to alert SRE when >X credits are consumed within first 10s of a tenant job. Linked internal ticket created: INT-581200 (telemetry-wave-detection).

Status: customer follows guidance and reports successful nightly runs with no data loss after splay. Marking issue for monitoring; will close once internal telemetry task is scheduled and config change validated in canary.
Workaround timeline: short-term splay implemented 2026-03-12 03:15 UTC; planned config change rollout targeted for 2026-03-20 in canary region.
